text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Liberal parliamentarian Meshari al-Osaimi withdraws a request to question Justice Minister Mohammad Sharar, also an elected MP. Some 30 MPs held an unofficial six-hour meeting on Saturday to convince Osaimi to retract his request.
- Sharar questioning withdrawn as part of tactic to focus parliamentary efforts on publicly questioning Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan.
- Kuwait presents prisoners of war issue at a public relations conference in Finland. Kuwait says Iraq is still holding about 600 Kuwaitis since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis. Baghdad denies the claim.
- Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah returned home after attending the Brussels Conference on Global Ban on Antipersonnel Mines.
- Egypt and the Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development on Saturday signed in Cairo a $50 million loan accord.
- Parliamentary committee introduces draft law to increase salaries at Kuwait University.
- Gulf Arab customs officials meet in Riyadh to discuss facilitating regulations and procedures.
- Iraq will not participate in an Arab sports tournament to be held in Lebanon in July. Kuwait last week said it would withdraw from the event if Iraq was allowed to take part.
